title: Heart on Fire Emoji ❤️‍🔥 Meaning: Passion or Burned?
description: The ❤️‍🔥 heart on fire emoji means burning love, lust or obsession, and sometimes a romance going up in flames. See how to read it from a crush or an ex.
summary: The ❤️‍🔥 heart on fire emoji means intense, consuming love or desire: a crush that won't cool down, strong physical attraction, or obsession with a song, show or person. Less often it marks the opposite, a love that burned out or a past that someone is deliberately torching.
meaning: Most people send ❤️‍🔥 to say a feeling is running hot. It is a step up from the red heart: where ❤️ says “I love you,” this one says “I can't stop thinking about you.” It turns up under thirst-trap selfies, in anniversary captions, and in late-night texts where plain affection would undersell the mood. Lust is part of its vocabulary, and the keyword list that ships with the emoji includes both “love” and “lust,” so reading it as flirtatious is rarely a mistake.

Fandom adopted it as quickly as couples did. Stan accounts drop it under a new album, a match-winning goal or a red-carpet look to mean “this is consuming me.” Nothing romantic is implied in that setting; the flame is enthusiasm. Fitness and motivation posts borrow it the same way, as a heart that is fired up, sitting in captions about training blocks, product launches and comebacks.

A darker reading exists too. Because the heart is literally burning, some people post it after a breakup to signal that they are setting the past alight, or that a relationship went up in flames. Others use it for love that hurts: the situationship you know is bad for you but keep returning to. Context does nearly all the work. Next to a couple photo it is desire; next to a joke about deleting someone's pictures it is arson.

There is a religious echo as well. A flaming heart is an old image in Christian art, where the Sacred Heart is shown burning, and “sacred” is among the emoji's official keywords. A small number of users post it in that devotional sense, usually beside 🙏 or ✝️. Technically the emoji is a combination, a red heart joined to a fire emoji, which matters for how it displays on older software.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Getting ❤️‍🔥 from someone you are flirting with is about as unambiguous as hearts get. It signals attraction with a physical edge, closer to “you look incredible” than “you're sweet.” As a reply to a photo it is a compliment on how you look. If the two of you are not at that stage, it can feel like a jump, and a softer heart usually lands better early on.

contexts.label: In a relationship
contexts.body: Long-term couples use it to say the spark is still there: date-night photos, anniversary posts, a text sent from the other side of a work trip. It tends to appear when one partner wants to sound less routine than the daily ❤️. Paired with a number, as in “6 years ❤️‍🔥,” it reads as pride that things have not gone lukewarm.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: In comments it is fan currency. It lines up in rows under edits of actors, musicians and athletes, and under any video where someone looks good or performs well. Creators also put it in captions for dance clips, gym progress and outfit reveals. Here it means “this is hot” or simply “this is great,” and nobody treats it as a declaration.

contexts.label: After a breakup
contexts.body: Posted alone on a story with a moody song, ❤️‍🔥 can mean a heart that got burned, or a person burning the bridge on purpose. Friends reading it will look at everything around it: a glow-up selfie suggests moving on with confidence, while sad lyrics suggest the fire did real damage.

examples.meaning: The date went very well and the attraction is strong, with a clear physical undertone.
A flirtatious compliment: you look extremely good in that outfit.

examples.text: Three years and you still do this to me ❤️‍🔥
examples.meaning: An anniversary message saying the passion has not faded with time.
A fan is overwhelmed by how good a piece of music is; no romance involved.
The sender is burning the memory of an ex and wants you to know they feel good about it.

examples.text: He's a walking red flag but ❤️‍🔥
examples.meaning: They know the person is trouble and are drawn in anyway.

combos.meaning: Overheated by how attractive someone is; a sigh of “I need a minute.”
Openly lustful. Reserved for people you are already flirting with.
Devotional use, pointing to faith and the image of a burning sacred heart.
A short story in two symbols: it burned, and now the healing has started.

confusedWith.difference: ❤️ is steady, all-purpose love you can send to a partner, a parent or a friend. ❤️‍🔥 adds heat and urgency, which makes it romantic or sexual by default and a strange choice for family chats.

🔥 on its own praises a thing: an outfit, a track, a play. It says “that's hot” or “that's excellent” without involving your feelings. Adding the heart makes the message personal, about what the thing does to you.

The two were released together and often get mixed up at a glance. ❤️‍🩹 shows a bandaged heart that is recovering; ❤️‍🔥 shows a heart in the middle of the blaze. One is the aftermath, the other the event.

avoid: Skip it with coworkers, clients and anyone who could read sexual interest into a message where you meant none.
Do not send it in sympathy for a real loss or illness; a burning heart looks like excitement, not comfort.
Hold off in the first messages with a new match unless the conversation has already turned flirtatious.
design: A red heart with yellow and orange flames rising from its top and sides. Vendors generally keep the heart whole and glossy, with fire wrapping around it instead of consuming it, which is why it reads as passion more than destruction. The emoji is built from three parts: ❤️, an invisible joining character, and 🔥. Apps that do not support the sequence show a heart and a flame side by side.

faqs.q: What does ❤️‍🔥 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually that he is strongly attracted to you, with more desire in it than a plain red heart carries. If he sends it in reply to a photo, treat it as a compliment on your looks. From a male friend commenting on your gym progress or new car, it is simply loud approval.

faqs.q: What does ❤️‍🔥 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: The same range applies. Sent privately to someone she is seeing or flirting with, it signals passion. Sent in a group chat or under a friend's post, it is the hype version of a heart, the kind of thing friends leave under each other's selfies without any romantic meaning.

faqs.q: Is the heart on fire emoji positive or negative?
faqs.a: Positive in most messages: desire, excitement, devotion. The negative use, a heart that was burned or a love that turned destructive, is real but less common, and it normally comes with other clues such as breakup lyrics or bitter wording.

faqs.q: Why do I see a heart and a flame as two separate emojis?
faqs.a: Your device or app does not recognize the combined sequence, so it draws the two ingredients individually. The sender saw one emoji. Updating the operating system or the app normally fixes it.

faqs.q: When was the heart on fire emoji added?
faqs.a: It was approved in Emoji 13.1 in 2020, in the same small release as the mending heart ❤️‍🩹. Both were created by joining existing emojis together, so no new code points were needed.
